issues.detail: The Greek 'προελθων μικρον' means 'having come forward a little' (referring to the distance he moved toward the disciples). The Vietnamese 'đi trước một chút' translates to 'went ahead a little bit' or 'walked a little further,' which changes the spatial relationship/direction of the movement.

The Greek 'παρελθη απ αυτου η ωρα' means 'the hour might pass from Him' (the hour passing by/away from Him). The Vietnamese 'xin giờ này qua khỏi Ngài' translates to 'please let this hour pass [past] Him,' which can be interpreted as the hour passing *by* Him or moving past him, but misses the specific Greek sense of the hour departing *from* Him.
